title: Find Champion I
statement:
A tournament has `n` teams labelled `0` to `n - 1`, described by an `n x n` matrix `grid` of 0s and 1s. For two different teams `i` and `j`, `grid[i][j] == 1` means team `i` is stronger than team `j`, and `grid[i][j] == 0` means team `j` is stronger than team `i`.

A team is the **champion** when no other team is stronger than it. Return the champion's label.

The input guarantees that `grid[i][i] == 0`, that `grid[i][j] != grid[j][i]` for `i != j`, and that strength is transitive (if `a` is stronger than `b` and `b` is stronger than `c`, then `a` is stronger than `c`), so exactly one champion exists.
constraints: grid[i][j] != grid[j][i] for every i != j
Strength is transitive: if a beats b and b beats c, then a beats c
notes:
## Intuition

The champion is the team nobody beats. In a complete tournament every pair has a winner, so "nobody beats team `t`" means team `t` beats every one of the other `n - 1` teams: its row holds `n - 1` ones. Enumerating the teams and counting each row's ones finds it directly.

## Approach

1. For each `team`, count its `wins`: the number of 1s in `grid[team]` (the diagonal is 0, so it adds nothing).
2. If `wins` equals `n - 1`, this team beats everyone else, so return it.
3. Transitivity guarantees such a team exists; `-1` is only a fallback.

## Example 1, step by step

`grid = [[0, 1], [0, 0]]`, so `n = 2` and a champion needs `1` win. Team `0`'s row is `[0, 1]`, giving `wins = 1 = n - 1`, so the answer is `0`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each of the `n` rows is scanned once at most.
- Space: O(1): only a counter.

## Pitfalls

- `grid[i][j] == 1` means row team `i` is the stronger one; reading the matrix as columns returns the weakest team instead.
- Do not count the diagonal as a win; it is always 0 here, which is why the sum works.
- Only one team can have `n - 1` wins, so returning the first match is safe.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of teams |
| `team` | the team being tested as champion |
| `other` | the opponent whose cell is read |
| `wins` | how many teams `team` is stronger than |

narration.2: There are n teams, one row and one column each.
narration.3: Try every team as the possible champion.
narration.4: Start counting how many teams this one beats.
narration.5: Read every cell of the team's row.
narration.6: A 1 means this team is stronger than other; the diagonal adds 0.
narration.8: Beating all n - 1 other teams means nobody is stronger.
narration.9: So this team is the champion.
narration.12: Unreachable for valid input; the guarantees ensure a champion exists.
